newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: First Bosnia genocide suspect pleads not guilty.
newsitem.headline: First Bosnia genocide suspect pleads not guilty.

text.p: A Bosnian Serb arrested by British troops earlier this month pleaded not guilty to a charge of genocide at the U.N. war crimes tribunal on Wednesday.
Milan Kovacevic, seized in an operation in which another suspected war criminal was shot dead by elite SAS soldiers, is the first person accused of genocide to appear at the tribunal.
"On the counts of this indictment, I am not guilty and God and the justice of this court willing, I think I will be found not guilty," he told the panel of three judges.
Kovacevic is accused of helping set up camps where Moslems and Croats were raped, tortured and killed during a brutal Serb "ethnic cleansing" campaign in northwest Bosnia in 1992.
The indictment against him said conditions in the Omarska, Keraterm and Trnopolje camps were appalling and brutal.

"Bosnian Serb military and police personnel in charge of these facilities, their staff and other persons...killed, sexually assaulted, tortured and otherwise physically and psychologically abused the detainees in the camps," it said.

Kovacevic and Simo Drljaca -- who was shot dead after opening fire on the British troops sent to arrest him -- were described in the indictment as members of the Serb Crisis Staff in the Prijedor region which established and controlled the camps.
The operation to arrest them marked the first time that NATO-led troops in Bosnia had actively hunted down war crimes suspects, of whom more than 60 remain at large.
Bosnian Serb hardliners have since launched a retaliatory series of explosions against international peacekeepers.
